reviews.title: Phantastic Cooling & Display ❄️🖥️
reviews.comment:
I’ve been using the Phanteks Glacier One 360M25-LCD in my main build to cool a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, and overall it’s a solid AIO. Performance-wise, this cooler does its job very well. I saw a noticeable drop in temperatures compared to my previous AIO, and it stays stable during longer gaming sessions and heavier workloads. Installation was straightforward, and the build quality feels solid. The display is excellent and clear from any angle, making it a great visual addition to the build. It can also be used in either a horizontal or vertical orientation, which adds flexibility depending on your setup. It’s not magnetic, so be mindful of how you mount the pump depending on whether you want it vertical or horizontal. Video playback seems to be capped under 80MB, and another feature that would be cool is the ability to use it as a secondary monitor screen function.
The limitation is the software at the moment. You're limited in what data you can display.
Available Display Options:
CPU and GPU temperature
CPU and GPU fan speed (RPM)
Pump speed (RPM)
I hope they can add more features in future updates, such as RAM usage, liquid temperature, CPU load, and GPU usage. Overall, I really like the large, vibrant display, and I think that overshadows the limitations of the software for me.
reviews.author: Mr. Next Level

reviews.title: Phanteks best AIO on the market right now
reviews.comment: The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/B1laVcAxWSL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/71dP0jwxgfL._SY256.jpg The quality of this AIO is top notch from top to bottom. From the screw covers on the fans that make it that much more appealing it is a great touch along with the daisy chained connections for the fans themselves making it easier to setup. As for the screen it is a nice big screen for displaying videos (max length is 56 seconds). There is also some customization options to choose from not the most but enough for a solid display setup if going with the simple picture setup. The fans also have the infinity design to them with the mirror effect which is a nice upgrade from standard plastic fans. As for noise levels they are nice and quiet but a headset is probably the way to go if gaming, also haven’t heard any noise from the radiator pump either. Lastly if you are having any issues with the display not updating it is likely a software issue from the app so just make sure everything is up to date. Overall though so far I haven’t had any issues with this setup and it’s keeping my Ryzen 7 7800X3D nice and cool when gaming on max settings. I just wish if you have a video playing you could also display the widgets without having to split the screen.
